name: Alak
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: Sidwell, Paul & Pascale Jacq. 2003. A Handbook of Comparative Bahnaric, vol. 1: West Bahnaric (PL 551); Sidwell, Paul. 2000. Proto South Bahnaric (PL 501); Schiering, René & Harry van der Hulst. 2010. Word accent systems in the languages of Asia (in van der Hulst et al. eds).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Alak appears only as lexical comparanda / in the classification list; generic remarks that Bahnaric words are sesquisyllabic with a stressed main syllable (PL 551 p. on WB) are not about Alak. No Alak-specific stress statement.

sources.note: Bibliography only. Alak items: Thomas 1979; Johnston, Saul & Thomas 1978 Alak wordlist (ms.); Prachakij-karacak 1995 [1919] wordlists; L-Thongkum 1997; L-Thongkum 2001 (Thai, 670 pp; ch.5 Bahnaric, ch.6 sound changes); L-Thongkum 2001 ms 'Is the Northwest Bahnaric sub-branch a fact or fiction?'. sources.note: No prose statement (classification paper, 'broad phonetic transcription'). Alak forms again carry the stress mark on the last syllable: ha'peet, ka'tap, ka'tiiŋ, pa'haj, ki'neh, n'tuuŋ (pp.100-105).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x reference list for alak1253 (12 refs); Wikipedia 'Alak language'; RWAAI (Lund) Alak > Miller Collection (4 wordlist-elicitation recordings, 12-14 Nov 1998).
sources.note: No phonology content; no grammar, sketch or phonology reference for Alak in Glottolog; RWAAI holds audio wordlists only.

sources.citation: Theraphan L-Thongkum. 1997. The place of Lawi, Harak and Tariang within Bahnaric. Mon-Khmer Studies 27: 109-117.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No prose statement. Harak (=Alak) data, 680 words, Ban Kasang Kang, Lamam district, Dec 1995; states 'Harak does not have vowel length distinction' (p.112). All disyllabic Harak forms are transcribed with the stress mark before the final (main) syllable: ka'tap 'egg', pa'dam 'five', ti'poh 'seven', ba'hac 'sand', ki'piu 'buffalo', ha'nam 'year' (Table 3, p.112) -- implicit final stress only.

sources.citation: Thomas, David. 1980 [issue dated 1979]. The place of Alak, Tampuan, and West Bahnaric. Mon-Khmer Studies 8: 171-186.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Lexicostatistical/lexical/phonological-correspondence classification paper using SIL Alak wordlists (Pakse); only prosodic remark is that Alak 'appears to have' register (p.179). scanned a full-text search for stress/accent/syllab: no hits.

sources.citation: Huffman, Franklin E. 1971. Field notebook 17, 'Cahier (Analysis)': (1) Souai (Laos), (2) Alak, informant Kham Koeng Khothavong, Pakse, March 1971. Franklin E. Huffman Papers, SEAlang Archives (36 handwritten pages).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent on stress. pp.2-28 rhyme-sorted Alak vocabulary; pp.29-33 prose analysis of CONSONANTS (tense /p t c k ʔ/ vs lax aspirated /p' t' c' k'/ that 'condition a very considerable high onglide in following vowels.. through all vowels of disyllables having a lax initial'), CLUSTERS (CC- vs CVC- has 'a morphological function'), VOWELS ('All vowels occur both long and short'), and a register discussion. No statement on accent/stress placement; 'disyllable', 'first syllable', 'second syllable' used without prominence remarks.
